analysis:
Both changed files are test-only Swift code under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests. No production code, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, authorization, cache crypto or coordinator contract is modified.

SegmentedFleetGeometry.swift (head lines 45-49): the gpt-oss-20b fixture dtypes change from [bf16 + 23x fp32] to 24x bf16. The new comment says the SDK's expert SwiGLU keeps bf16, so every layer stores bf16 K/V. This affects only the admission and pool config fixtures (admissionConfig, poolConfig). It changes the expected KV sizing in tests and does not change production behavior. The fixture now assumes production no longer stores fp32 K/V rows for gpt-oss. That depends on a production or SDK change outside the supplied evidence. If it is wrong, the tests would under-price native admission, and the effect would be availability or capacity mis-sizing (GPU memory pressure, T-029 class) rather than confidentiality. It is a test-fidelity question, not a demonstrated regression.

EngineV2PrefixCacheWiringTests.swift (head lines 435-436, 445): comment-only edits. The expectations are unchanged (nominal + 2048 for contiguous GPT-OSS with no native dtypes; nominal for paged). The comments now describe the fp32 delta as a conservative fallback when native types are unobserved. This touches no code in the T-041 affected files (EngineV2SlotFactory and others).

No new attack surface and no change to the SSD prefix-cache threat posture (T-041, SEC-035). The next pass should confirm that the production seam in EngineV2SlotFactory/EngineV2Factory that produces native layer dtypes for gpt-oss matches these fixtures. That seam is outside this batch.
